newsitem.title: UK: London precious metals eyeing stocks for guidance.
newsitem.headline: London precious metals eyeing stocks for guidance.

text.p: Gold prices steadied after an early bout of selling on Thursday and the market's attention was glued to financial markets for direction.
Prices dipped about $1.00 in early trading to a low around $368 an ounce on moderate selling rumoured to originate from a gold producer, dealers said.
"But a few people liked it down there, and it had a modest bounce when bargain hunters came in," a dealer said, noting that the gold had found support around $368 an ounce.
Bullion was fixed at $368.60 an ounce, compared to $368.25 on Wednesday afternoon and $369.60 in the morning.
Volumes were relatively thin and trading subdued so far compared to the volatile trading seen in recent days.
In the near term, dealers said, movements in the stock and bond markets would rule gold's roost.
Last Friday gold briefly soared to nearly $375 an ounce when a shake-down on Wall Street sent investors scurrying to the precious metals.
European bourses were mixed and nervous so far, after renewed fears about interest rates caused a sharp fall in U.S. stocks on Wednesday.
The dollar was slightly stronger, but traders were waiting for U.S. consumer price figures due later in the day for clues on the health of the American economy.
"Maybe 30 percent of the focus is on the metals and the other 70 percent is on the financial markets, where selling could trigger movement in this market," a dealer said.
"There's a good chance of a rally in precious metals should financial markets make a serious reversal."

Otherwise, however, the market was still bearish overall since tumbling to three-year lows last week on concerns about selling by producers and central banks combined with slack physical demand. Some analysts forecast a drop to $360 an ounce.
Silver and platinum were closely shadowing gold and were indicated little changed from London's closing levels.
Silver was unchanged at $4.82/$4.84 an ounce, while platinum was up $0.25 at $368.50/$369.50.
Palladium, which had been edging up steadily this week, was slightly easier at $118.75/$119.75.
The white metals may have more potential on the upside than gold should the yellow metal stage even a modest rally, dealers said.
